summary:
OUTPOST is an interactive educational space survival simulator in which you're tasked with the experience of setting up a human settlement on the Moon. You're the outpost commander and it's your job to keep your crew alive by managing the vital resources of oxygen, water, food and energy.

The project is about making space exploration and the engineering challenges of living off Earth more engaging and accessible. You do this by having the player build the key systems, keep their crew safe from the hazards of the environment, deal with the unexpected emergencies and make the hard calls with very limited resources.

OUTPOST is key as it takes the rather dry subject of space science and turns it into an engaging learning experience. It's a platform where students can get their heads around resource management, sustainability, the trade-offs involved in engineering and the process of problem solving in general. It's a great way of stimulating interest in the idea of living on other worlds. It's all inspired by actual NASA research.
details:
Imagine waking up one day on the Moon.

There's no supermarket, no hospital in the vicinity and no regular delivery from Earth.

Every breath you take, every drop of water you drink, every meal you eat and every unit of electricity you consume is dependent on the systems that you've built.

So how would you survive?

That's the question that underpins our project OUTPOST: Humanity's Next Frontier.

OUTPOST is an interactive educational space survival simulator in which the student takes on the role of an astronaut commander tasked with setting up a lunar base.

Players will need to build the basic infrastructure, manage their resources (which will be very limited), look after their crew and deal with the various environmental emergencies that will crop up at short notice.

But there's a problem in that every decision has consequences.

A greenhouse produces food but it requires water and electricity. An oxygen generator will support life but will also consume resources. Solar panels provide power but are subject to the vagaries of the weather.

Through all of these challenges the student learns that space exploration isn't just about getting to another planet. It's about creating the systems that will allow humans to survive there.

Our aim is to take the complex world of space engineering and turn it into an exciting experience which will stimulate curiosity, creativity and problem solving.

We see OUTPOST being expanded to include further missions (Mars, more sophisticated sims etc) and a range of co-operative educational challenges.

Because the next generation ought to be learning about space exploration.

They should have the opportunity to go through its trials.

OUTPOST. Build. Survive. Explore.
